source_text: Οὐ γὰρ τοῖς πολλοῖς φέροντες ὑμᾶς αὐτοὺς ἀνεμίξατε, οὐδὲ πλήθει τὴν εὐσέβειαν ἐμετρήσατε, οὐδὲ δῆμος γενέσθαι μᾶλλον ὀχλώδης ἠνέσχεσθε, ἢ λαὸς Θεοῦ λόγῳ κεκαθαρμένος· ἀλλ' ὅσον εἰκὸς, Καίσαρι τὰ τοῦ Καίσαρος εἰσενεγκόντες, τῷ Θεῷ τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ προσενείματε· τῷ μὲν τὸ τέλος, τῷ δὲ τὸν φόβον· καὶ τὸν δῆμον τοῖς ὑμετέροις θρέψαντες, ἥκετε καὶ αὐτοὶ παρ' ἡμῶν τραφησόμενοι. Σιτοδοτοῦμεν γὰρ καὶ ἡμεῖς, καὶ σιτοδοσίαν ἴσως τῆς ὑμετέρας οὐ φαυλοτέραν. Δεῦτε, φάγετε τὸν ἐμὸν ἄρτον, καὶ πίετε οἶνον, ὃν κεκέρακα ὑμῖν· καλῶ μετὰ τῆς σοφίας ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν τράπεζαν. Ἐπαινῶ γὰρ τῆς εὐγνωμοσύνης, καὶ προστρέχω τῇ προθυμίᾳ, ὅτι ὡς ἐπὶ λιμένα ἴδιον ἡμᾶς κατηντήσατε, τῷ ὁμοίῳ προσδραμόντες, καὶ τὸ συγγενὲς τῆς πίστεως ἐτιμή σατε, καὶ τῶν ἀτόπων ἐνομίσατε, τοὺς μὲν ὑβριστὰς τῶν ἄνω συμφρονεῖν ἀλλήλοις καὶ συναρμόζεσθαι, καὶ τὸ καθ' ἕκαστον σαθρὸν οἴεσθαι διορ θοῦσθαι τῷ κοινῷ τῆς συστάσεως, καθάπερ τῶν σχοινίων τὰ τῇ πλοκῇ δυναμούμενα, αὐτοὶ δὲ μὴ συνιέναι, μηδὲ συνδεῖσθαι τοῖς ὁμογνώμοσιν, οἷς γε εἰκὸς μᾶλλον· αὐτοὶ γὰρ συνάγομεν καὶ θεό τητα. Καὶ ἵνα γε εἰδῆτε, μὴ μάτην προσδραμόντες ἡμῖν, μηδὲ ὡς ξένοις καὶ ἀλλοτρίοις, ἀλλ' ἐν ὑμετέ ροις καταχθέντες, καὶ καλῶς ὁδηγηθέντες ὑπὸ τοῦ Πνεύματος, βραχέα περὶ Θεοῦ φιλοσοφήσομεν ὑμῖν. Καὶ γνωρίσατε τὰ ὑμέτερα, ὥσπερ οἱ τοῖς ἐπισήμοις τῶν ὅπλων τὸ οἰκεῖον διαγινώσκοντες. Ηʹ. Δύο διαφορὰς ἐν τοῖς οὖσι γινώσκω τὰς ἀνωτάτω, δεσποτείαν τε καὶ δουλείαν· οὐχ ἃς παρ' ἡμῖν, ἢ τύραννις ἔτεμεν, ἢ πενία διέστησεν, ἀλλ' ἃς φύσις διώρισεν, εἴ τῳ φίλον οὕτω καλεῖν. Τὸ γὰρ πρῶτον, καὶ ὑπὲρ τὴν φύσιν. Τούτων δὲ, ἡ μὲν ποιητική τέ ἐστι, καὶ ἀρχικὴ, καὶ ἀκίνητος· ἡ δὲ πεποιημένη, καὶ ὑπὸ χεῖρα, καὶ μεταπίπτουσα. Καὶ ἔτι συντομώ τερον εἰπεῖν, ἡ μὲν ὑπὲρ χρόνον, ἡ δὲ ὑπὸ χρόνον. Καλεῖται δὲ ἡ μὲν, Θεὸς, καὶ ἐν τρισὶ τοῖς μεγίστοις ἵσταται, αἰτίῳ, καὶ δημιουργῷ, καὶ τελειοποιῷ· τῷ Πατρὶ λέγω, καὶ τῷ Υἱῷ, καὶ τῷ ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι. Ἃ μήτε οὕτως ἀλλήλων ἀπήρτηται, ὡς φύσει τέμνεσθαι· μήτε οὕτως ἐστένωται, ὡς εἰς ἓν πρόσωπον περιγράφεσθαι· τὸ μὲν γὰρ τῆς Ἀρειανῆς μανίας, τὸ δὲ τῆς Σαβελλιανικῆς ἀθεΐας ἐστίν· ἀλλ' ἔστι, τῶν μὲν πάντη διαιρετῶν ἑνικωτέρα, τῶν δὲ τελείως μοναδικῶν ἀφθονωτέρα. Ἡ δὲ μεθ' ἡμῶν τέ ἐστι, καὶ καλεῖται κτίσις, κἂν ἄλλα ἄλλων ὑπεραίρῃ, κατὰ τὴν ἀναλογίαν τῆς πρὸς Θεὸν ἐγγύτητος. Θʹ. Τούτων δὲ οὕτως ἐχόντων, ὅτῳ μὲν ἡ καρδία πρὸς Κύριον, ἴτω μεθ' ἡμῶν, καὶ προσκυνῶμεν τὴν μίαν ἐν τοῖς τρισὶ θεότητα, μηδὲν ταπεινότητος ὄνο μα τῇ ἀπροσίτῳ δόξῃ προσάγοντες, ἀλλὰ τὰς ὑψώσεις τοῦ ἑνὸς Θεοῦ ἐν τοῖς τρισὶ διαπαντὸς ἐν τῷ λάρυγγι φέροντες. Ἧς γὰρ οὐδὲ μέγεθος φύσεως κυρίως ἔστιν εἰπεῖν, διὰ τὸ ἄπειρον καὶ ἀόριστον, πῶς ταύτῃ ταπεινότητα ἐπεισάξομεν; Ὅστις δὲ ἀλλοτρίως ἔχει Θεοῦ, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο τέμνει τὴν μίαν καὶ ὑπὲρ πάντα τὰ ὄντα οὐσίαν εἰς ἀνισότητα φύσεων, θαυμαστὸν, εἰ μὴ τῇ ῥομφαίᾳ τμηθήσεται, καὶ τὸ μέρος αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀπίστων τεθήσεται, πονηρὸν δρεπομένου πονηρᾶς δόξης καρπὸν, καὶ νῦν καὶ ὕστερον.
thought_title: Right tribute to God and the two kinds of beings
orientation: Gregory praises the Egyptian visitors for true piety and then begins his concise teaching about God and creation.
pass_a_gloss: For you did not mix yourselves by bringing yourselves to the many, nor did you measure piety by multitude, nor did you endure to become a mob-like crowd rather than a people of God cleansed by the word; but, as is fitting, after paying in to Caesar the things of Caesar, you assigned to God the things of God; to the one the tax, to the other the fear; and after feeding the populace with your own things, you yourselves also have come to be fed by us. For we also distribute food, and a food distribution perhaps not inferior to yours. Come, eat my bread, and drink wine which I have mixed for you; with Wisdom I call you to my table. For I praise you for your gratitude, and I run to meet your eagerness, because you landed upon us as upon your own harbor, after running to what is like, and you honored the kinship of faith, and you counted it among absurd things, that the insulters of the things above should agree with each other and be fitted together, and should suppose that the rottenness in each case is corrected by the common alliance, just as with ropes the parts strengthened by twisting, while you yourselves should not understand together, nor be bound together with those of like mind, to whom this is more fitting; for we join together even divinity. And so that you may know, that you did not run to us in vain, nor as to strangers and aliens, but were landed among your own things, and were well led by the Spirit, we will discuss briefly about God for you. And recognize your own things, just as those who discern what is their own by the devices on weapons. 8. I know two highest distinctions among beings, lordship and servitude; not those among us, which either tyranny cut, or poverty divided, but those which nature distinguished, if it is pleasing to someone to call them so. For the first is also above nature. Of these, the one is productive and originative and unmoved; the other is made and under hand and changing. And to say still more briefly, the one is above time, the other is under time. And the one is called God, and stands in the three greatest, cause and maker and perfecter; I mean the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit. Which are neither so detached from each other as to be cut in nature; nor so contracted as to be circumscribed into one person; for the one is of Arian madness, the other is of Sabellian atheism; but it is more unifying than things wholly divided, more bountiful than things completely singular. And the other with us is and is called creation, even if some things surpass others, according to the proportion of nearness to God. 9. And since these things are so, whoever has his heart toward the Lord, let him come with us, and let us worship the one divinity in the three, bringing no name of lowliness to the unapproachable glory, but bearing always in the throat the exaltations of the one God in the three. For of whom it is not strictly possible to speak even greatness of nature, because of the boundless and indefinite, how shall we introduce lowliness to this? But whoever is estranged from God, and for this reason cuts the one being above all beings into inequality of natures, it is no wonder if he will be cut by the sword, and his portion will be placed with the unbelieving, while reaping an evil fruit of an evil opinion, both now and hereafter.

pass_b_english: For you did not cast yourselves in with the many to follow the crowd, nor measure devotion by numbers, nor consent to become a noisy mob rather than a people of God purified by the Word. As was right, you rendered to Caesar the things of Caesar, and you assigned to God the things of God (Matthew 22:21): tribute to the one, reverence to the other (Romans 13:7). After feeding the populace from your own stores, you yourselves have come to be fed by us. For we too hand out food, and a food distribution perhaps no poorer than yours: "Come, eat my bread, and drink the wine I have mixed for you" (Proverbs 9:5). With Wisdom I invite you to my table.

I commend your gratitude, and I run to meet your eagerness, because you have put in to us as to your own harbor. You hastened to your like, you honored the kinship of faith, and you judged it absurd that insulters of what is above should agree with one another and fit together, each supposing that what is rotten in him is repaired by their common alliance, like strands made strong by twisting, while you yourselves should fail to come together and be bound to the like-minded, for whom it is far more fitting. For we bring even divinity itself together. So that you may know you have not run to us in vain, nor landed among strangers and outsiders but among your own, well guided by the Spirit, I will speak to you briefly about God. Recognize what is your own, as men recognize their own by the devices on their shields.

I know two highest distinctions among beings: lordship and servitude, not those that tyranny has carved among us or poverty has divided, but those that nature has marked off, if one wishes to call it that. For the first is even beyond nature. The one is productive and ruling and unmoved; the other is made and under authority and subject to change. To say it still more briefly, the one is beyond time, the other is under time. The one is called God, and stands in the three greatest: cause and maker and perfecter, I mean the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit. These are neither so detached from one another as to be cut apart by nature, for that is the madness of Arius, nor so contracted as to be confined into one person, for that is the atheism of Sabellius. It is more united than anything wholly divided, and more abundant than anything wholly single. The other order is with us, and is called creation, even if some stand higher than others according to their nearness to God.

This being so, let whoever has his heart toward the Lord come with us, and let us worship the one divinity in the three, bringing no name of lowliness to that unapproachable glory, but always carrying in our throats the exaltations of the one God in the three (Psalms 149:6). For if we cannot properly speak even of greatness of nature, since it is infinite and unbounded, how shall we impose lowliness upon it? But whoever stands estranged from God, and therefore cuts the one being above all beings into an inequality of natures, it will be no wonder if he is cut in two by the sword and his portion is set with the unbelievers (Matthew 24:51), reaping an evil harvest from an evil doctrine, both now and hereafter.
